note:
Additional field evidence from #2546 arm 2 p5_fits, same file, same problem space: the poller's log-staleness arm is STRUCTURALLY BLIND during a fan-out phase, so the CPU-advancing override is the only thing keeping the verdict right.

Observed 2026-08-27 during a healthy p5_fits fan-out:

  poller watches      /workspace/logs/issue-2546.log
  workers write to    /workspace/issue2546/work/fits_a2/slot0..3.log
  result              last_log_mtime_sec_ago = 2134 while all four workers were computing
  verdict             correct, but ONLY via the #518/#658 CPU-advancing override

So during fan-out the poller has no real progress signal at all; it infers liveness from session
CPU. That is exactly the inference this task is asking you to put a rate floor on, which makes the
two halves interact: if the override gains a floor but the staleness arm stays blind, a fan-out
phase whose workers ALL wedge would present as stale-log plus low-CPU and be indistinguishable
from the phase simply being between log writes.

Suggested addition to the same fix, at your discretion: let the poller take a progress signal from
the per-worker slot logs (newest mtime across a phase's worker log glob) rather than only the
dispatcher log. That converts the fan-out case from CPU-inference back into direct evidence.

## The rate separation, now measured in the OTHER direction too

This task's original evidence was the wedge side (~0.9 CPU-sec/min). Here is the healthy side of
the same phase, measured on a cumulative basis over a ~1800 s window:

  session_cpu_secs   9,040 -> 58,455   =  ~1,650 CPU-sec/min  =  ~27 cores sustained

Against the deadlock's ~0.9 CPU-sec/min that is a ~1,800x separation, wider than the ~65x I
originally reported from the single-core refit. A rate floor has an enormous margin to work with;
the sign test has none.

Also confirmed here: GPUs idle is NOT evidence of trouble on this phase. The poller posted its
gpu-idle advisory (all 4 GPUs idle 30 min during healthy phase=p5_fits) while the phase was
verifiably healthy at ~27 cores, because P5's fits allocate no CUDA context at all (0 percent AND
0 MiB across 8 samples over 56 s). The separate plan-side defect that causes it is filed as #2624;
noting it here only so a future implementer does not treat GPU idleness as a wedge term.

Do NOT touch the live #2546 arm-2 pod.
